proof.h2: Did you know the New Testament quotes the Book of Enoch?
proof.jude: And Enoch also, the seventh from Adam, prophesied of these, saying, <mark>Behold</mark>, the Lord <mark>cometh with ten thousands of his</mark> saints…
proof.enoch: And <mark>behold</mark>! He <mark>cometh with ten thousands of His</mark> holy ones To execute judgement upon all…
proof.thread: In Greek, the two passages share about 72% of their words
body: This prophecy closely matches the opening chapter of the Book of Enoch — a book most Bibles in the West don't include, but the Ethiopian Orthodox Church has kept in its Bible.
That's the kind of discovery you'll find in The Ethiopian Codex: not rumors, but texts you can check for yourself.
proof.source: Jude 1:14 (KJV) · 1 Enoch 1:9 (trans. R. H. Charles, 1917) · both public domain

items.title: Why 81 Books?
items.desc: How the Ethiopian Bible was formed, and why it has more books than yours. "The 81 books" is the Church's own name for its Bible — and different lists reach 81 in different ways.

items.title: The Book of Enoch
items.desc: The Watchers, the Nephilim, the seven archangels named in chapter 20, and Enoch's journeys through the heavens.

items.title: The Book of Jubilees
items.desc: The "Little Genesis": Genesis retold, week by week of years — and what it adds to the stories you already know.

items.title: Found Only in the Ethiopian Bible
items.desc: Including the three books of Meqabyan, which are not the Maccabees you may know.

items.title: Fact or Hype?
items.desc: 10 viral claims from the internet, each one judged with sources.

items.desc: A 30-day reading plan, a glossary, "Echoes in Your Bible" and the full bibliography.
